analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/configuration.md: the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and the `backend.enabled_models` row (line 201). The supplied units are base_text excerpts at lines 485-949, which cover the SSD prefix cache and MiMo, cluster, and environment-variable sections. None of those lines are changed. The patch excerpt is truncated, but its range map is complete and lists only lines 3 and 201.

The documented behavior change is that a background `start` now saves the complete selection to `backend.enabled_models`. A nonempty list acts as an operator filter on coordinator `load_model`, `prefetch_model` and `desired_models`. Unless Autopilot is on, the filter blocks loads, downloads and advertisement of models outside it. `operatorFilterAllows` in ProviderLoop+ModelSelection.swift is cited as the reader.

This is a restriction, so it is tightening, not new attack surface. It relates to TB-002 (coordinator-to-provider control messages) and to T-012/T-027 only indirectly. The code is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot verify it. Open questions are whether the filter fails closed when the list is malformed, and whether it covers the 'selected build's alias successor' path. The doc says a hand edit applies only at the next start, which is a documentation-level staleness point, not a vulnerability.

The base excerpts show no security-relevant documentation contradicting the changed row. Prefix cache, SSD KEK and debug-key-file documentation is unchanged and still consistent with T-041 (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE, 30-minute TTL, HMAC names). No findings. Deeper review is unnecessary for this docs-only change; the Swift implementation is outside the supplied evidence.
